utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Ms. Somers, you are to call a further witness now, I believe. If you would call the case for hearing. We'll have the case called first. I was jumping ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-42-T, the Prosecutor versus Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The Prosecution will call as its witness Lars Jensen Brolund.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, only briefly: My colleague, Mr. Petrovic, still has to correct Exhibit number 10, or rather, add the translation, and this is ready now, in connection with the cross-examination of Mrs. Alajbeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to say, Mr. Rodic, that I didn't have my headphones on, and by the time I got them on, you had finished. So I'm not sure what it was that you were putting to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague, Mr. Petrovic, during his cross-examination of the previous witness, Mrs. Alajbeg, still had to add a translation into English of Exhibit number 10, and this is the translation now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Rodic. Now if Mr. Brolund would take the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you would be seated. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name for the Court.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I have to make a little correction to my statement. My full name is not Lars Brolund but Lars Jensen Brolund.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brolund. Would you indicate your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: 26th of December, 1953.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what is your nationality, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm Danish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which languages do you speak?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I speak Croatian, English, German, and some Russian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Brolund, in the course of this examination, we will be speaking in the English language. I am aware that it is not your first language, and I will attempt to go slowly and clearly, and I would ask you, if there is a question about anything I have asked you, if you would please ask to have it repeated or clarified.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Brolund, if you could give us a little bit of your background. What was your profession in 1999, let us say from the middle of 1991, I'm terribly sorry -- until the end of 1991, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time I was working as a clerk at the local administration body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you have military service in your background? Were you a member of the military of Denmark?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I was at that time, and I still am a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is your rank, please, Mr. Brolund?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm a first lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you a first lieutenant at the time in 1991, let us say in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time, I was contemporarily promoted into the grade of major, when I was serving at the European Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did you come to serve with the European Community Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I volunteered. I made a telephone call to the Danish army and asked if it would be possible for me to be a member of the mission, and I was accepted as a member of the first Danish group to go down as part of the mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you have some background in the region and/or with the language at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Besides my degree in law, I had also a bachelor degree in Slavonic languages, that is, in Russian and B/C/S, and I had been studying B/C/S at university, together with Russian, and I had been dealing rather much with Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the interests of time, I may simply ask you to give a little bit of a background, perhaps a bit more quickly, since it appears you are able to understand the questions. When did you actually go to the former Yugoslavia as part of the monitoring mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was on the 17th of July, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And at what point did you go to the Dubrovnik area?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I arrived to the Dubrovnik area for the first time on the 5th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And where were you with the mission before you arrived at Dubrovnik? What were your placements? Where were you located?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As you know, the headquarters of the mission was in Zagreb, and during the first months of the work of the mission, we had our taskings in Slovenia and in Croatia as well, so I had taskings in different parts, some Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you aware what had taken place in Slovenia and Croatia in June of 1991?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I had been following that rather detailed, because I had to go down to attend a language course in Ljubljana, Slovenia, from about the 1st of July, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what happened? Did you in fact attend the course without any difficulty, or what was your experience there at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I made a request, because of the situation, through the telephone, and I was told that the course would take place, and therefore I went down to Ljubljana by train at the end of June 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the situation at the time, as you understood it? What had happened?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, at that time, as far as I remember, the 25th of June, 1991, Slovenia and Croatia had declared their independence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated, I believe, that you were in Zagreb. Now, did you at some point have an assignment to the Dubrovnik area? When did it begin, if you did?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let me repeat it. I'm sorry if I perhaps complicated it for you. When did your assignment in the Dubrovnik area actually start?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As I said a little before, I arrived to Dubrovnik for the first time on the 5th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I take a moment to bring the Chamber's attention, and perhaps I should seek to have it admitted at this time. Mr. Brolund, you have, in the course of your work in Dubrovnik on the mission, did you keep notes that were made either at the time or contemporaneously with your work? Did you keep notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I have here by me some parts of my diary and personal notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Personal notes we are not interested in, but notes that relate to the work of the mission, did you keep those notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I have them here with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you provide copies of them to the Office of the Prosecutor when you gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And have you reviewed the copies that were given, and can you indicate they are the same copies of the same notes that you personally took during the course of being a monitor in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have been able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask, in order to facilitate the following by the Chamber, that we first of all circulate the exhibit, which is from the 65 ter list. I won't worry about the 65 ter list number, but I will ask that it be identified by the ERN 02187221 et seq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This should be given a number now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P21.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Brolund, the document which is in front of you, Exhibit P21, is that in fact -- does that represent a copy of the notes? It should be -- is it on the screen as well? It is also on your computer screen as computer evidence, if it would assist you. Are these the same notes that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor and that came -- that were made by you personally?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I note that in the course of them, there is a mixture of the Danish language and the English language, and as a result, an attempt was made to have a translation from Danish, which we have discussed is not very satisfactory. It has some gaps, as you have seen and pointed out to us as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Because of that, we would, of course, try to have a better translation provided, but for the purposes of today's testimony, I may ask you, when referring to something in your notes that may have gone into your statement, if you could be kind enough to read it and then offer us into English what may be in the Danish or what may be unclear to the person who translated or attempted to translate. Are we agreed on that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes, certainly. That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'll ask that this be moved into evidence -- I'm sorry. I assume with the issuing of a number, it has been.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Brolund, what was your essential assignment? What were some of the component parts of your assignment as a monitor? What were you there to do?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, as the name itself of the mission tells, we were there to monitor. And according to the agreement made between the parties, first and foremost, to monitor the ceasefire, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, you were in Zagreb initially, but when you got down to Dubrovnik, was there a different headquarters for the area that covered Dubrovnik? Was there a regional headquarters?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So at the middle or from the end of October 1991, the mission established original headquarter at Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In Dalmatia?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you -- who was the head of the regional centre in Split, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The head of the regional centre in Split was the Italian ambassador, Mr. Bondioli.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when you make reference, if you do make reference to Mr. Bondioli throughout your diary, any parts of it, how do you indicate he is the person you're referring to? Do you have an initial -- what is your way in your notes of indicating that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I used the initial B and a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: B. B as in boy?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tell us, please: How did you get to the Dubrovnik area? What was your actual route? And how long were you there the first time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We went by -- we would go out to the coast, to the little town of Crikvenica, and from there, we went by ship. We did think that we had to go to Split, but on the 4th of October, we learned that we had to go to Dubrovnik, where we stayed until the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you able to -- would you have been able to have gotten to Dubrovnik on land?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why would that be?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Because the traffic routes simply were disinterrupted [sic] because of the military operations going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the situation in the harbour of Dubrovnik? Was it -- was open entry possible? What was the situation there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As far as I remember, at that time the blockade of the coast was already established.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when you came into Dubrovnik, did you have to go through that blockade?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Well, I can establish that there was a blockade already at that time, because we had to get clearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where are you reading from? Are you reading from your diary?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Could you indicate to the Chamber, please, the page. It would be okay, I believe, just to indicate the number at the top. It would have an 02 something number. Which page are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Page -- the first page, 02187221.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you got into Dubrovnik, where were you accommodated?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We were accommodated at the Hotel Argentina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who else, if anyone, was accommodated there? I'm sorry. Let me just ask you. Was that for the entire mission? Were all ECMM accommodated there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: There were also accommodated some refugees there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you do upon your arrival? What was your first official obligation in the Dubrovnik area?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At first we had a meeting with a crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And is that a Croatian organisation?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What level were these -- what level were these people? Were they from the area or from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: They were from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, on the 5th of October, can you indicate whether or not something occurred while you were walking along to your hotel. Did something happen that was worth discussing here?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, there was a little episode with some shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Shelling from where, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seemed to us that the shelling came from the sea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And shelling by which forces, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we were not -- we couldn't see anything, so we were in fact not able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you do in response to the shelling?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We immediately -- my colleague, Leif Maersk and I, fell to the ground to get shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where did the shells land, if you had to fall to the ground? Why did you fall to the ground?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: They were landing relatively close to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you reading now from your notes? If so, could you indicate the page.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. The page is now 02187221.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How long were you on the ground, if you know? If you can remember?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So about five minutes. I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: During your stay in Dubrovnik, did you ever -- during the first stay in Dubrovnik and that would be up till the 10th of October, did you go behind JNA lines?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. We were trying to establish contact with the JNA authorities, but we did not succeed in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And so your initial contacts during that time were with the Croatians?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just a quick question: Are you familiar with a feature called Srdj?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And can you just tell us what it is and perhaps where -- what it represents to you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it's an old military object in the mountains, just above Dubrovnik. It dates, as far as I know, back to the Napoleon wars.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, do you know who was holding Srdj, which forces were holding Srdj?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you observe anything happening to the cross on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. One day during my first stay in Dubrovnik, there was an air attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: By which forces?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that it can only be the JNA air force, because the Croats didn't have any air force at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was the result of this air attack? What happened, if you remember, or if it's in your diary?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the big cross was destroyed on the -- the big cross on the mountains above Dubrovnik was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you left Dubrovnik on the 10th, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We went back by boat to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you do in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time, I had leave. We arrived at Zagreb on the 12th of October, and the same day I left Zagreb by train, to have leave in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did you arrive back in the theatre of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I arrived again at Zagreb on the 20th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you go back to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not at once. At that time, the mission was going to establish its regional centre at Split, and so the same day I was also sent to Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did you get to Split, if you can just quickly tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Also by boat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: From which city?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: From Rijeka, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, what was the purpose, what was the first thing you needed to do, or you were supposed to do, when you got there? What was your first official function on the 28th of October?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: On the 28th of October. Well, according to my notes, I had some taskings already on the 21st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And they would have been what?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was, according to my diary, some meetings in a little town called Zitnic, near Drnis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After you completed that particular tasking, did you go to attend a meeting on the 28th of October?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the nature of that meeting, and what was the purpose of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was a meeting with General Strugar at Meljine, in the Boka Kotorska and it was a courtesy call.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: A courtesy call. Are you able to indicate the page from which these entries would have been drawn in your diary, in your notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. The first page is 02187223.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, looking at that page, and again, apologising for the quality of the English -- attempt at an English translation, I'm going to ask you about the meeting. Can you tell us, please, who was present at that meeting? My specific question is: Was it -- was there a Croatian presence, or if not, who?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, there was no Croatian presence. Present were the following persons: From the JNA side, General Pavle Strugar, Frigate Captain Jeremic, Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic, and Lieutenant Colonel Svicevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where was the meeting held?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was held at some military barracks at Meljine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And where is Meljine?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: In Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did you get to Meljine from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We went by boat from Split, into the harbour of Herceg-Novi.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And from there, how did you get to Meljine?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: With some vehicle, which I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you remember any recollection of where in Meljine the meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I haven't. Only that it was at some military object.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You mentioned four names. You mentioned Pavle Strugar, Svicevic, Jokic, and Jeremic. Are you able to tell us from your understanding at the time what forces, in other words, was there a break-up of land forces and naval, and if so, who was who?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Pavle Strugar and Svicevic did belong to army forces, and Jokic and Jeremic to the navy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you have any indication from anything at that meeting who was leading the meeting, who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It appeared that General Strugar was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What factors made you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, he was sitting so at the middle of the table, on his side of the table, and he was doing most of the talking from that side, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was your -- most of the talking. What types of topics were discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: According to my notes, our ambassador, Bondioli, did explain something about the work of our new regional centre at Split, which had just been established, and about the work of the monitoring mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was present from the mission with you? You said Mr. Bondioli. Was there any other monitor?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bondioli was the leader of our team, and present was also Mr. Haupt and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was the -- were the remarks of General Strugar addressed as - you describe him chairing the meeting - addressed to your head of delegation?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. So I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In your various minutes that we have, do you make any indications when you refer to General Strugar, how do you indicate that he either commented or spoke in your minutes? What do you use?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I indicate that with the initials G.S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That is, where you have not specifically spelled out the full name of Strugar, you use his initials; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Throughout this document which all of us have, where we see G.S., that means General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us a bit about the nature of the discussion there? What topics were brought to the table?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, Mr. Bondioli told something about the work of the regional centre and monitoring mission as such, and then there were also discussed some points sent by General Strugar to the mission and the Croatian side about the situation in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sent by General Strugar? In other words, General Strugar was discussing points about Croatia -- the Croatian...?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that document. It was signed by General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say "document," what are you referring to when you say "points about Croatians"? What was the subject matter? Where were these points contained?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it contained several proposals, that was the word used, how the situation in the Dubrovnik area could be solved, according to different problems. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you for just a second? I would ask, please, that the usher distribute copies of the next exhibit I wish to tender, which -- it is in both B/C/S and in English. It bears ERN in the Serbo-Croatian language 01846651, with the English translation commencing with 01846652. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, the word here used is that it's some propositions for the normalisation of life in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And was this document discussed at the meeting in Meljine, at which General Strugar was present, on the 28th of October?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask that -- to tender into evidence the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P22.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at the document that you have before you - and you have it both in your hand, and I believe it would also be on the screen - do you remember the discussions that concerned this document at the meeting? Can you tell us a bit of what was said?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall in my memory much of what was said at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you make notes of it? Are these contained in your diary?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I have notes about that contained in my diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please refer us to the numbers of those pages so it will assist us in following.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The first page is 02187224, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Before we get into any of the actual text of the document: Was there -- let me go back for a second. Who raised the issue of the contents of this document? Where did the discussion come from? Who brought it up at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I really don't remember, and I'm not even able to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase this so that you're familiar with -- so that we go back and it's clear to you. What was the nature of this document? Can you tell us what it represented? And who put the document out?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? Who put --?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Whose document was it? Who actually put out this piece of paper that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Whose signature -- whose name is under the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, the document is signed by Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So the name Strugar appears -- Pavle Strugar appears at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Albeit I don't know that there's a signature, but his name is under the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, did General Strugar discuss this document at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Both Svicevic and Admiral Jokic and General Strugar made comments in different ways on these points.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, what Mr. Svicevic said about the document.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: He told that it was -- he said that it was a big misunderstanding concerning that he told that the army had not put any ultimatum, but just some propositions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Proposals. Okay. And I think you had indicated that he had said he had not given. Was there a correction in the transcript about the translation of what Mr. Svicevic said that you wished to make? Did he say that does not give ultimatums or has not?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it's formulated a little differently in my statement, and I have to correct that a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Because he did not speak generally, but only about these 11 points, where he said that the army had not given these 11 points, put any ultimatum, but just some proposals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And in the Serbo-Croatian language, what is the word that is actually used?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The word is "Predlozi."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that would translate to?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Proposals, propositions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at the document, I'd like to do a quick run-through with you. And what was the purpose of these, as it were, proposals? What were they trying to achieve, according to the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: According to its own wording, it was to achieve the normalisation of life in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And anything else? Is there anything else that's indicated there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And securing the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is the date on this document, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The date is the 27th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That is at the end I see 27. What date is at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, at the top of the document, the date is the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And to whom was this document actually addressed?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was addressed for the members of the EC mission and the crisis headquarters of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Also referred to as the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Point 1 of the document reads -- are you able to take a look and just assist us in going through it very quickly? What is point 1 of the document, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Point 1 is that all the weapons situated in the zone of Dubrovnik should be surrendered to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the Croatians ever do this? Did they ever agree to do this as of that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The second point?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The second point is that the JNA controlled the surrender of the weapons with the EC Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was that something that the ECMM agreed to undertake? Were they going to ever assist in the collection of weapons?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did that happen with ECMM?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Third, please.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That members of ZNG and MUP of Dubrovnik were not residents of Dubrovnik since before January 1st, 1991 had to leave the area of the municipality of Dubrovnik. The JNA guarantees their safe leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did that occur?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. I couldn't acknowledge that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That all foreign mercenaries should be surrendered to the diplomatic representatives of their countries, who will deport them from Yugoslavia. The JNA guarantees their safe leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did that ever happen, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Number 5.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That the MUP should be brought in to the states as of January 23rd, 1991, and responsibility and independently regulate the peace and respect of the legal norms in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Responsibly and independently regulate the peace and respect of the legal norms in Dubrovnik; is that what that says?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Could you please explain first before I ask you a second question about that. What is the MUP? What does MUP mean?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: In fact, that is the police. These letters mean Ministarstvo Unutrasnjih Poslova, the Ministry of Interior affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what is the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That is Zbor Narodne Garde, a military formation put up by the Croats at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did point number 5 materialise? Did it happen? Did it occur?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Point number 6.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That all signs of political parties should be removed from public places on the area of the municipality of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did that occur?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Number 7.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The JNA guarantees an absolute ceasefire of its members and the security of the citizens, and Dubrovnik with its cultural and historical monuments.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Its cultural and historical monuments are acknowledged in this document, then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that the JNA would protect or guarantee the security of those monuments. Was that your understanding of that point?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, as one of these 11 points.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not that came to pass? Did that occur?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems to me that the opposite did happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Point number 8.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Armed formations of the JNA not to enter Dubrovnik on the line from the crossroads one kilometre west from the village of Dupac to settlement Mokosica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not that occurred?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Number 9.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: JNA to organise the control of entrance and exit from Dubrovnik in order to safe the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Entrance and exit to and from Dubrovnik. What was the reality of who controlled entrance and exit to and from Dubrovnik at that time anyway?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time, Dubrovnik was already encircled and blocked, both on land and from the sea.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: By?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: By the JNA and the JRM.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Point 10, please.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As soon as possible, the JNA will provide to the appropriate working organisations of the city of Dubrovnik the supply of electricity, water, PTT connections and other accompanying infrastructures and economic functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, when they refer to the city of Dubrovnik in this particular context, are we also including the Old Town, the old centre of town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So it appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, please, what was your observation, having lived through it, of the state of infrastructure at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: When we were there at the beginning of October, there were already no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What about at this point in time? We're now talking about the 28th of October. What was the situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Still no electricity? Was there still no electricity?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, at that time, I had not myself been in Dubrovnik from after the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: After you -- after this meeting, did you then go into Dubrovnik, and did you determine what the state of the infrastructure was about this time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. After having finished the meeting with General Strugar, we went into Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was the state of the infrastructure? How were things with water, electricity, et cetera, necessities?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: In fact, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Point 11 on the second page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: All these conditions are valid until the final agreed solution of the Yugoslav crisis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So does it appear that these conditions are tied to a more global Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. set of events than just what is happening in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, so it appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When was the reply to this expected? What does it tell us?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, according to the last sentence, a reply was expected by October 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, this -- at a particular time? Does it give you a time? October 27th, and is there a time indicated?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes. At 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, you are meeting on 28th of October. What time did your meeting start, approximately?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm not able to establish that in my notes, and I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: All right. But the date of October 28th is after October 27th, do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, did it appear to you from the discussions at this meeting that there had been a response or compliance from the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It appeared to me that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was the atmosphere that you felt about this at the meeting, that you felt from General Strugar, Admiral Jokic? How did that manifest itself, that this had not had a response?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, according to my notes, Admiral Jokic - that's in the middle of page 02187225 - proposed a detailed examination of the 11 points and an answer from the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was General Strugar's comment, if any, about the points that are called here proposals or propositions?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: On the same page, I have a note that General Strugar said that these points were of only humanitarian character, so they were no ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did there come any discussion -- I'm sorry. Let me just ask another question about this. Now, did General Strugar ever talk about whether or not he was acting outside of the political network, or what did he say about the politician side of things?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. He said something about that, and two occasions during -- or more; I have noted two occasions during the meeting. On page 02187224, about the middle, I have noted that he said that his side will just implement the political will, and will not do anything on its own, that it is subordinated military commands in Belgrade and Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you explain. Belgrade may be clear. What was the relationship in Zagreb? What was there of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Because the Peta Vojna Oblast, the 5th Military District.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Of the JNA, was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you happen --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry. Excuse me. Do you happen to recall if there was a JNA liaison person? If you recall, in the 5th Military District? Do you know? To the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. General Raseta.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you hear from General Strugar as to his relationship to the -- what is referred to in your statement, but I believe more specifically referred to in your notes as the SSNO? If you could tell us, please, where that is found.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. He said also something about that. It was later during the meeting, on page 02187226. There was a break in the meeting, and after that, according to my notes, General Strugar stressed that he was strictly obeying orders from the SSNO, that is, the federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of what entity? Of what?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, a quick point of clarification. When you make reference to Admiral Jokic in your notes, if you do not specifically spell out Jokic, how do you indicate that it is something that he has said? What was your abbreviation or notation for Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I use the abbreviation ADM point, and a big G point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: J?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: A big J point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was there any discussion about the JNA soldiers firing on the Croatians? Was there anything that the general himself discussed with your delegation about the nature of firing activity by the Croatians?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I have something about that also in my notes. Yes. It was also at the same time during the meeting when General Strugar stressed that he was obeying orders from the Ministry of Defence. He said a little later that projectiles, fire, not directly threatening soldiers from the Croatian side should be tolerated. The first time, the second time, the third time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And where is that in your notes? If you could give us the page, please.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It's also on the page 02187226.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I note that the 1, 2, three times did not make it into your statement. Are you correcting it now to indicate that it was first time, second time, third time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. So it was said, according to my notes, so I have to correct that also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And then what would happen after the first time, the second time, the third time, as General Strugar indicated to you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I understood it so that the first three times, it might be tolerated, but then fire would be answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, as of the 28th of October, 1991, had you been aware of the JNA already firing or shelling or engaging their weaponry against Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember from our first visit to Dubrovnik at the beginning of October that we were shown some impacts at the Old Town walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you had made reference, I believe, to some air engagement.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have already mentioned the attack -- the air attack on the cross, and I have also mentioned the episode with shelling we had personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you observe Admiral Jokic making any comments about this, or was it just General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is it in your notes that anything said by Admiral Jokic on this, or was it restricted to General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At this point, I cannot recall that Admiral Jokic said anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I will move on, then. Can you indicate whether you had any observations about the relationship between Admiral Jokic and General Strugar that you might have gotten from that meeting, in terms of who commanded whom?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, as I have said already, it appeared that General Strugar was leading the meeting, so it appeared that he was the first in command and that Jokic was subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How long have you been in the military -- had you been in the military at that point in time? How many years? How many years had you been a soldier at the time of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I did active military service from 1973 to 1975, as a conscript, and as a conscript, I also received the education as a reserve officer. And after that, I was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you still a reserve officer today?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I have still a contract with the Danish army as a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And in the course of your military exposure or training, are you able to get a sense of when subordination is evident? Can you tell, as a soldier, when someone is subordinate to someone else? Is it apparent by a number of factors?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Often it will be apparent in some ways, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Going back to that meeting, do you recall a discussion about an upcoming, actually, the next day, meeting of some ambassadors that was to take place, and if so, if you could tell us where that might be found in your particular diary.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have some notes about that too. On page 02187226, almost at the top, after the first two lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is said, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I must say that I don't remember that from the meeting. I know it only from my notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. What do your notes tell you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: They tell that on the 29th of October, there should be a meeting with some ambassadors and military attaches. They should land at Tivat airport at 8.45 and arrive at Dubrovnik at 12.00. And until 1.00, there should be sight-seeing, and then lunch at Tivat. According to my notes here, they should be brought to Dubrovnik by a warship, or yacht.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you participate in that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I did not learn anything more about that visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, when it was discussed at that meeting in Meljine, was General Strugar present with this discussion about this ambassadorial group?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, he was present, and during the entire meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move on. I'd like to move to a time in December of 1991. Now, you were still in Dubrovnik. Up until what point did your second tour of duty keep you in Dubrovnik? When did you leave Dubrovnik from your second tour of duty?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So you mean after the meeting on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Dubrovnik the second time? When did you end your time in Dubrovnik, generally? We finished with the meeting on the 28th for now. In general, how long did you find yourself staying in Dubrovnik with the mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm a little confused, because the second time I went to Dubrovnik, it was after the meeting with General Strugar. It was only for a short time, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Only for a short time in Meljine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, and then we went to Dubrovnik for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And how long? How long were you there in Dubrovnik that next time? Why don't you tell us this, so it's not confusing: After the meeting in Meljine, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We went to Dubrovnik and stayed there, according to my notes, until the 29th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And then what? What did you do on the 29th of October?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Then we went back to Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you return from Split to Dubrovnik at some point?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When was that, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was on the 4th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And how long was that time? How long did that period, that tour of duty in Dubrovnik last? Until when?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Our team left Dubrovnik again on the 8th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And -- okay. We'll take it to that point now. Now, what was the purpose of your returning to Dubrovnik on the 4th from Split?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The purpose was that our team should escort a delegation of Croatian ministers for some negotiations with JNA authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, Croatian ministers. Are these people local from the Dubrovnik political area or are they from another place?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. They were members of the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And where were they based out of?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So they must have been based in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you go to Zagreb to meet them, or where did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We met them in Split, and escorted them from Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, the names of these ministers, if you have it also in your notes, if you could help us with that.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I have that, on page 02187231. The leader of the delegation of ministers was Davorin Rudolf, and the other members were the minister of commerce, Kriste and the minister of environment, as far as I remember, Sifric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know of what ministry Mr. Rudolf was minister?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It was sea communications, sea connections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Maritime?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Maritime matters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What, if anything, may have occurred to you about -- let's stop for a second. What were they going to do? What was the purpose of these ministers coming to the Dubrovnik area? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that they were going to have some negotiations with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, what, if anything, about the fact that they were cabinet-level persons may have struck you? What went through your mind?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, of course that indicates that it's some very important negotiations and important matters to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know -- were you ever given any indication of what types of matters were to be discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we were told that, among other things, they had to discuss how to solve the situation around Dubrovnik, about lack of electricity, lack of water, and how to lift the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was held at the little town of Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is Cavtat on the water? Is it on the water? Is it on the coast?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did you all get there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: By our boat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you -- again, were you part of the group that went in to discuss matters? Were you included in the group, at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. We were told that we were not going to be present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And do you recall the date of the meeting that it was scheduled for? When was the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. We arrived at Dubrovnik on the 4th of December, and the meeting was on the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you yourself do not know what was actually discussed inside that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not, from the indications of the ministers, whether or not the meeting resulted in an agreement, or was there to be some additional meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It appeared that no agreement was made. As far as I remember, there should be another meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who, if you know, was representing the JNA at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember after the meeting that Admiral Jokic appeared.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you see General Strugar at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you see any of General Strugar's -- any of the people who were present at the first meeting that you mentioned on the 28th? Were any of those persons at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was your understanding of what was to happen as a result of that meeting? Was there any discussion about when there would be a continuation of discussions?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that, but, well, I had the impression that there would be another meeting soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you know -- were you aware of the day that there would be a rescheduled meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking -- now, where were you on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We were in our hotel, Argentina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And can you describe, please, the events of the 6th of December. Was there in fact any noticeable improvement in the situation in Dubrovnik then?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. On the opposite. I wake up -- according to my notes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you tell us the page, please, so that we can try to --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. That is page 02187231. I have noted, and I remember very well also, that early in the morning, about 6.00, heavy shelling began on Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That was the time you first heard heavy shelling, or shelling?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was your reaction? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I was shocked, of course, as everybody else in the team. It was unclear to me. There had been some negotiations, and then suddenly shelling began. And I took a look out on the sea to establish -- try to establish where the shelling came from. I couldn't see anything. And so I went down to our operation room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where was the operations room?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was in the lowest etage [sic] of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where I building was that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was the building of Hotel Argentina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was going on there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At our operational -- operation room, the leader of our team, Mr. Hvalkof, was already sending messages to Split about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof. Now, what country is he from?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: He's a Dane.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you work together during a good portion of the time in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. During these days, from the 5th until the 8th of December, we were there together as members of the same team.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was ECMM attempting to do from that room?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We were sending our reports to our regional centre in Split about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there any observation on your part as to whether the Croatians were surprised about this attack? Did you speak to any of the Croatians that you had been dealing with, let's say, the day before?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Hvalkof and yourself, did you record --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Now I remember that Mr. Rudolf was also present at our operation rooms, and as far as I remember, he was shocked too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was Mr. -- If you remember, what was his reaction? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: He tried to contact the -- as far as I remember, he tried to contact the other side in order to get information about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you document, through your diary, to the best of your ability, what occurred in the way of the reaction of the people in Dubrovnik and what was happening with the shellings? Did you record that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have some notes about that, how the shelling continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which page could you direct us to?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It is still the page 02187231.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And can you take us through that? I think you're best able to give us the times and what it was you observed?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. So about 6.00 in the morning, the heavy shelling began, and then at 7.15, according to my notes, there was a general alert.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What is a general alert, please?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, a high sound of a siren.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: A siren?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: A siren.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And at 7.20, at least two impacts in the Old Town, at 0732 until now 1011, impacts in the old town. At 0845 hours, impacts fell close to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Hotel Argentina?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Our hotel window was broken. The hotel hit by at least one shell, a lot of broken glass on the corridor outside my room. At 0920, our boat to Cavtat, Argosy II with the EC flag on it, directly hit in the old harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And the old harbour is where in relationship to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It's immediately at the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there damage done to your boat, the Argosy II?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Both that boat, Argosy II, and also Argosy I, burned totally out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And then between 0930 and 0945, intensified shelling upon the Old Town. At 0945 until 1000, about 10 to 15 heavy explosions per minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Still in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And anything about the harbour?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Upon the Old Town, the old harbour also, and the island of Lokrum.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And then at 1045, still shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, during this period where you are describing the shelling coming into the Old Town, can you indicate whether you at any time observed any outgoing fire from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At any time during your stay in Dubrovnik, the first time, the second time, the third time, did you observe any outgoing fire from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In other words, you don't remember seeing it, or you did not observe?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, in fact I didn't see it. I didn't observe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Going back to your page where you have an entry for 1500, if you could assist us, please.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have noted at 1500 hours, shelling still going on, though Admiral Jokic sent excuse.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And to whom was the communication from Admiral Jokic sent?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you receive any other communications from the JNA during that time? Let me just go back for one second. An excuse about what? What was the excuse, if you remember generally?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember, but the only logical thing would be that it was an excuse because of the attack, because of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you recall if any other communications came from the JNA side that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have noted at the 0710 hours that a letter was received from General Strugar, where he was writing that the Croatian forces had not respected the ceasefire. And so the damage upon the Old Town was in fact because of their own fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can I just ask, please, at this moment to ask the usher to assist us with distributing the next exhibit I would seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P23.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at what has just been labelled Exhibit P23, what is that document in front of you, please? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You know the contents? Do you recognise the contents?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems to be the same document which I am mentioning in my papers, in my notebook, but I'm not able to recognise it as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But you -- the content of it. Let's look at the content of it. Does it match what you have just told us was said by General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it matches that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough just to read it, the time, the date, if you can, please, if it's clear enough on the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The English text is as follows, from JNA Boka to Davorin Rudolf, minister: "The JNA forces were attacked, with no apparent reason, by the mortars and machine-gun fire this morning from Srdj and from Babin Kuk. Our forces answered to the fire. At 1115, our units ceased the fire under my commandment, but your forces" - excuse me - "did not observe the ceasefire. That is why it can be concluded that the buildings in the Old Town were damaged by your forces, General Colonel Pavle Strugar."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, I note the time on this may differ a bit. I think you said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. I'm terribly sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The time on this reads 1714. You have an approximately 1710. Is this still the same communication, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, please: In your minutes, in your notes from your diary, where do you address this particular document? So that I can just make sure I'm on the same ...

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It's on page 02187231, at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, I note at the bottom, it actually appears to be in English, and you have some punctuation, as it were, some notations at the end of it. What is the purpose of those what appear to be exclamation points? Why did you put them there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I put them there because it seemed to me that the content of the letter was pure nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And are you able to give any indication why you so viewed it?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it's completely unlikely that the Croats themselves would inflict such damages on Dubrovnik themselves. That is evident for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, would this be a convenient time to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be, indeed, and we will break, therefore, for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Brolund, returning to the points you were making about the shellings on the 6th of December. I note that your statement, and I believe your diary, makes reference to something called a wire-guided missile. Can you please discuss what you meant by that and what your observations were of such wire-guided missiles during these attacks?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I have, also concerning that, to make a little correction to what is quoted in my statement. It's correct that I noticed such wire-directed missiles, how they went past -- they went -- they passed by in the air, our hotel, towards the sea. And I remember that one of these wires fell down on a tree outside the hotel, down towards the sea. But I must say at this moment, at least, that I can't recollect that I saw these missiles impact in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At the time of this statement, when you met with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, however, is it correct that you did indicate from your own recollection at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that that is what is in your statement?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That your statement says: "During the day, I observed the wire-guided missiles flying past us and landing in Dubrovnik, including the Old City." Was that your communication personally to the investigators at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it was. But, well, it's two years ago, and I must say today that I can't recall in my memory that I saw the missiles impact on the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I note in your diary, and also communicated in your statement, the mention of Trebinje. You indicated that you believe the majority of the artillery fire came from the land and possibly from the direction of Trebinje. Where is Trebinje, if you can just tell us?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It's a town located about 20 kilometres from Dubrovnik, above Dubrovnik. In fact, on the other side of the border, that is, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. From the time frame in your document, it appears that until relatively late in the day there was some shelling. Do you have an observation about what the reaction of the people of Dubrovnik was? Were they on the street? Were they in -- had they sought shelter? What was your -- if you know.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. I don't know, in fact, anything about the reaction of the population of Dubrovnik concerning the 6th of December, because we were not leaving the hotel at all that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Could you leave the hotel? Was it safe for you to do so?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seemed to us that it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Turning to the next day, that's 7th of December. What events occurred on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: According to my notes, on page 02187232, at 0915 hours, we went into the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which town would that be?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: The Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when you say "we," who was with you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So it was our team, Mr. Hvalkof and Mr. Hans Van de Beek, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what were your observations upon going into the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we could observe the big damages which had been inflicted, that there was broken glass, and broken roofing tiles everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
