utterances.text: Did you observe any serious damage? What was -- can you give us a description of what you saw, if you're able to do that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I brought a film to my camera and we went up in the church tower, at the Franciscan church, at the monastery, Mala Braca, which was also damaged by several shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: From the top of -- from the church tower, we could observe a lot of damage to roofs, and all over the town, and it seemed that almost every roof was damaged, and also of the old well near to monastery was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you able to make any observations as to whether or not the damage was restricted to one area, or was it broader?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems that it was not only restricted to one area; it was much broader.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you observe any, at that point, any, let's say, evidence -- a continuing evidence of either fire or smoke?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember any fire, but there was still a lot of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there were civilians who had been in the Old Town at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We learned that there were about 20 civilian casualties, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That may have been throughout Dubrovnik, correct, throughout all of Dubrovnik, not necessarily just --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm so sorry. What was -- what else, if you can tell us, please, occurred on the 7th?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before you answer that, let me just ask you this: Before you went into the Old Town on the 7th, had you been in the Old Town during that stay, during that trip, when you came the 4th, had you been in the Old Town before that, before the 7th, let's say between the 4th and the 7th?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I can -- I don't remember that today, but I can establish that in my notes on the page 02187231, at the 4th of December, at 1300 hours, arrival at Dubrovnik, in the afternoon, tour through the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The town meaning the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you, on the 7th, notice a difference in the condition of the Old Town than what you had seen on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Everything was completely different.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: On the 4th, there were, as far as I remember, very little damage, or little damage, compared with the situation on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, going back to what you were going to do officially as part of your duties again on the 7th, could you tell us, please, what was to happen?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. The delegation of the ministers did want to arrange a new meeting at Cavtat, and it was scheduled that the meeting should be at 12.00. Now, I am again on page 02187232, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know the purpose of the meeting? Who was going to attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, again, the delegation of the ministers, and then some of the commanders from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And these ministers would be the same persons you're talking about, that Mr. Rudolf, Mr. Sifric, and Mr. Kriste; is that true?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, did they in fact have a meeting at Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what was the role of ECMM at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At this meeting we were present because the meeting took place on board our ship, the UNICEF hydrofoil boat, Krila Dubrovnika.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You say it took place on board. Did you all come together? Did you and the ministers arrive together from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. We went away from Dubrovnik on board this boat together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the arrangement? How were you to get there? By what -- where were you to land?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was planned that the meeting should take place in a small town called Srebreno, probably. The way I have written it in in my notes is wrong, probably. I have spelled it like Srebrene.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is that a water location, a waterfront area?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you get to Srebreno?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. The boat couldn't go into the small harbour at Srebreno.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And because of that we went to Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you try get into the harbour at Srebreno? Did you attempt? Was there an attempt to get into the harbour?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I have written here, we could establish -- it appeared that the boat could not go into the harbour of Srebreno where Admiral Jokic and Frigate Captain Jeremic were already waiting on us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were Admiral Jokic and Mr. Jeremic waiting for you at the harbour, at the docking area at Srebreno?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. So it is written in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So what -- I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: And they said we could sail to Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when you got to Cavtat, what took place, and where?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Then the meeting took place on board the boat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The boat, the Krila Dubrovnika?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who presented the JNA at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: From the JNA at this meeting were present Admiral Jokic and Frigate Captain Jeremic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there any particular concern, if you remember, for security of the group that you were accompanying? Was there any security issue?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember -- or no. I can't say that I remember that. I know also that only because of my notes, that the Croats had some concerns about their security. It's on page 02187232, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was Cavtat occupied by the JNA at that point?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What in fact was discussed at that meeting, please? What were the points to discuss?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I have noted here that, and I remember also, that there was made an agreement, and I have noted here that there was made an agreement about Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. absolute ceasefire; gradual reduction of forces on both sides, should be arranged, should be negotiated; and deblocking of the harbour and the islands; and re-establishing other ferry traffic; and it should also be sought to establish again free road traffic; and as a fifth point, reparation of electric and water installations should be made possible, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated earlier that both the Croatians and you were surprised, I believe you used the term "shocked," about the events of the 6th. Did ECMM, either through you or any other monitor, make any protest or comment to the JNA about the events of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that Hvalkof, on behalf of our team, made a strong protest to Admiral Jokic, which I interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you get any sense of the admiral's reaction or from his response any sense of how he may have viewed the events of the 6th? If you can -- and if you did, can you explain your observation.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember that very well, and it seemed to me that he was not comfortable with the situation at all, as if he was sorry about what has happened, what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not a ceasefire in fact came into effect?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let us now turn our attention to the 8th of December. What happened on the 8th of December?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: In the morning, somewhere in the morning, we escorted some photographers, according to my notes. It's also page 02187233.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What kind of photographers?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Some photographers and intelligence agents, in inverted commas, from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did these photographers and intelligence agents get escorted by you, and where were they?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, they had -- an arrangement had been made with the Croats so that they could come in and inspect the damage, and inspect the damages in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So what you're telling us, if I understand it correctly, is that JNA officers came into Dubrovnik. Now, did they come in uniform?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And were they offered sufficient security during that visit?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems to me they were escorted by Croats and also by us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tell us, please, about what they did, about the tour, as it were, of the old city, of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, this walk through the town, as far as I remember, did last quite some time, and it seems to me that they inspected almost all the Old Town. We were on the city walls also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did they -- did you walk, as much as you can remember, around the entire area of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you walk around the entire area of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I can't tell you we went over the entire area, but a great part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did they speak, did persons from the JNA speak during the course of this tour?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, they did not speak much, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was it an obvious group, with much publicity, or was it more, shall we say, guarded?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was more guarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What -- do you know what, if anything, happened after these persons visited the Old Town? Was there any result that you were made aware of by the JNA, any action?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. In fact, I was not made aware of such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask you for a moment, please, to take a look at a series of four photographs that I would ask to be considered a composite exhibit. Mr. Brolund, do you recognise these photographs?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Because it's my photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You took them. I understood you took these photographs?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I took these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, they seem to cover -- they have different shots of things, and they may -- are they all from one day or do they vary? Do they have a number of days covered?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: They cover several days. Probably -- you see the first of them on page 02187235 is due to the text which I have written myself and taken from the backside of my photo. According to that, the photo is from the 5th of December, when we went to Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And does this show anything? I realise that it's a bit difficult because the quality is a little faded. Is that simply Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, with two JRM patrol boats.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And on the second photograph, what is depicted on the second photograph?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it seems to be some kind of homemade Croatian armoured vehicle, and my colleague, Leif Maersk, is also on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you say homemade, that is your description?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, in inverted commas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On the other page, please, can you indicate what the people are -- who they are and where these photos were taken? That would be on 02187 --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. On the next page, yes, on page 02187236, the upper picture is from the visit of the JNA representatives inspecting the damages and taking photographs on the 8th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who -- okay. These are the JNA persons in plain clothes. Are you able to indicate which of these persons is JNA? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Only the tall man to the left, in the white coat. He's a JNA representative.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The picture below, can you tell us, please, what that represents.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It's a picture taken in Cavtat on the 7th --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: -- of December, on board our boat, Krila Dubrovnika, during the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you able to identify some of the persons in this picture? If you can, I'll ask you to do so.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. So from the left side, at first, two of the Croatian ministers. It seems to be in front Sifric, and behind him, Kriste, and then in the background, standing, Mr. Hvalkof, from our team; and on his left side, Mr. Rudolf, sitting; and then to the right, the two representatives of the JNA, that is, the JRM. I'm not quite sure who is who, who is Jeremic and who is Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: From this picture, yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'll ask, please, for this to be marked. If I could ask for a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received as the one composite exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P24.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me just take one minute, Your Honour. If I may take one minute, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did you leave Dubrovnik altogether on this mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I left Dubrovnik on the 8th of December, at 10.00, before noon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when did you -- where did you go from there, please? From Dubrovnik, where did you go on the mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I went back to Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Croatia all together during this time period?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I stayed in Croatia until the 25th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And then what did you do after the 25th of December?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I went home to Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you finish your time as a European Community monitor?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Between the 6th of December and the time you left Croatia altogether, did you ever become aware, or was it ever brought to your attention, any attempt by the JNA into an investigation or discipline as to the events in the Old Town? Are you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I have no further questions at this time. Thank you very much. I just wanted to remind the Chamber of the issue with Mr. Brolund's having to depart tomorrow. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Somers. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a minor technical problem, Your Honours. Having in mind this remark made by my learned friend and colleague Somers, I wish to inform both her and the Chamber that the Defence will fully comply with this time limit in relation to Mr. Brolund. Our cross-examination is certain to finish by the end of this deadline. May we just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lars, my name is Goran Rodic. I am Mr. Strugar's Defence counsel. I will ask you questions on behalf of Mr. Strugar. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: First of all I would like to ask you the following: Before Yugoslavia, the former Yugoslavia, had you ever been on any other kind of military mission or other kind of mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that you had served in the Danish army and that you are a reserve officer. Could you please tell me: What sort of training did you go through during your military service with the Danish army, or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can tell you that I have got a special education for reserve officers at the special school of the Danish army, where I got an education in Russian. This education took place at a school which name at that time, when I became pupil in it, was called Teknikerliniens Befalingsmandsskole.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand you correctly. As part of your special training, you were taught Russian. I didn't quite understand what you being taught Russian has to do with your military training, the link between the two.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it's a special education for reserve officers in Russian and different military topics for military interpreters, and satisfies the needs of the Danish army to have the people speaking that language.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Which means that the specialty of the school where you were trained and the special training in the Danish army is teaching Russian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain any other forms of experience through your training, technical, infantry, artillery, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, certainly we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have any particular specialty within that framework?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. At the school we also had topics such as interrogation of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would I be correct in describing that school as some sort of intelligence school, in defining intelligence being one of the specialties you obtained once you had been through the training?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: You can say so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Having gone through the training of an intelligence officer - correct me if I'm wrong - you should be familiar with specialties that I have referred to, such as artillery, infantry, the different kinds of weapons used, and so on and so forth; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was the first time you visited the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was in July 1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me more about where exactly you were?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Modrica, near Sibenik, as a tourist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Sibenik, Vodice, Pirovac, Zadar, that area, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You visited all these places, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I didn't recognise all the names you mentioned; only some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of your first visit?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I was there as a tourist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that in 1979 and 1981 you had also visited Dubrovnik. Was that also a mere tourist visit?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask the counsel of the Defence to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In 1979 and 1981, were you in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was that also for tourism?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At that time, I was there on language courses, in 1979 and 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: After 1981, including 1991, how many other times did you visit the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I visited the former Yugoslavia several times during that period of time. In 1983 I was on a language course in Ljubljana, and 1984 also at the same language course, at the University of Ljubljana. In 1985, I was again there on a language course, which took place at Belgrade and Novi Sad and other towns. And then it must have been 1986 I was again in Dubrovnik as a tourist, on a charter trip. And then I was in Yugoslavia again in 1989, again on a language course, which took place in Belgrade and Zadar. And also in 1990, again at the University of Ljubljana, on a language course. And I was, as I have already told at the beginning, supposed also to attend the language course at the University of Ljubljana in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please tell us: Your university in Denmark, is that a university where you obtained your degree in Russian and Serbo-Croat at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In Denmark, in your own country, your university was the university where you obtained a degree in Russian and Serbo-Croat; am I right?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That was the university of Aarhus in Denmark, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This university, I assume you finished university upon the completion of your military service in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The purpose of all the trips you made to the former Yugoslavia, was it purely touristic or did it also have to do with education and improvement, learning, and for the sake of your spoken Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, as you have heard, I have mostly been on language courses and not so often on tourist trips, and so what I would like to do was to gain some better knowledge of the Serb -- of the B/C/S language and to learn something more about that beautiful country.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I assume that you were informed, in view of your knowledge of the language and your many visits, about the political and social structure of the country and how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, on the language courses, we were not, as far as I remember, told much about that. But I don't remember much about that. It seems to me that there was not much about the society and the structure of the society, but probably there was something.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I assume that you were interested in Yugoslavia as a country. I assume that you had some spare time to spend with people when you talked to those people, you probably talked to them also about the country in which you were staying, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I was talking with many people about many different things, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I assume that, in relation to an average Dane, your information about the former Yugoslavia was much higher, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I was much more interested in that country than most people in Denmark, so of course, yes, yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was the Serbo-Croat language a language used during your missions to Split, Zagreb, Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did often. I was used as an interpreter, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This probably means that when you talked to members of the JNA or the Croatian authorities in this period of time, on the discussion you probably used Serbo-Croat, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask the counsellor of the Defence to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This means you used Serbo-Croat in your talks with the representatives of the JNA and the representatives of the Croatian side during your stay in Zagreb, Dubrovnik, Split?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I have already told that I was working as -- functioning as an interpreter at several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In addition to your work as interpreter for the mission in the former Yugoslavia, did you have any other position or tasks as part of your work with the mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, in fact, my function was to be a monitor, and so accidentally, because of my knowledge, because I had some knowledge of B/C/S, I did function as an interpreter sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Prior to your arrival in Yugoslavia, or following your arrival, did you attend any briefing where you were informed about the situation in Yugoslavia and about what your own task would be?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We were briefed by the minister of foreign affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I assume the minister of foreign affairs of Denmark.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please briefly tell us what you were told there about the situation in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you not take any notes to be able to jog your memory as to what your task would be on the mission and how you would be representing your country and what your country's interests were in the situation?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I did not take such notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what specifically you were doing in Zagreb and how long you stayed.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I stayed in Zagreb from the middle of July 1991 and until, well -- so, in fact, until the 20th of October, when I went back -- when I went down to Split, to the regional centre at Split. After the 20th of October, I did not come back to Zagreb any more. But, of course, during the period, that period in Zagreb, I went at some occasions to other towns. I have already told here at the beginning how I went to Dubrovnik from the 5th to the 10th of October. And, for example, well, we had taskings all over Slovenia and Croatia, and I also went, for example, to Osijek, in Eastern Slavonia, somewhere about the middle of September. And I also went, for example, at the beginning of October, to Petrinja, in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What were your specific tasks on those occasions as a monitor?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, our main task was to monitor the situation, for example, to monitor the withdrawal of the JNA from Slovenia, and to report about that to our headquarters in Zagreb. After each tasking, the team would make its report. So the leaders of the mission reported back to -- at that time to The Hague here, because the Netherlands was -- had the presidency in the European Community at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you very much. Tell us, please, specifically: When monitoring the withdrawal of the JNA from Slovenia, did you encounter any problems? Was there anything special you noticed or anything special that you were informed about as part of your mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Also in relation to the JNA, did you monitor elsewhere in Croatia or in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Pardon? I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In Slovenia, you monitored the withdrawal of the JNA. My question is: In Zagreb, and elsewhere in Croatia, all the places that you have referred to, were you on any monitoring missions to do with the JNA? If so, please specify.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, at many occasions we had -- I was on taskings where we had contact with the JNA. For example, when I went to Petrinja at the beginning of October, and also when I went to Osijek in September, we had at that time liaison officers --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, in more specific terms, in view of your military experience and education and your previous visits to Yugoslavia, did you observe anything unusual, in your view, with regard to the JNA, as the legal armed force of that country?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So if I did observe anything unusual. How do you mean? In which aspects?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean in the period while you were in Croatia, was the JNA blocked in its barracks? Were they unable to leave their barracks, and did you find this unusual?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I am aware of the fact -- I remember that JNA was blocked in some barracks, or, as far as I remember, in some periods. And, well, because of the situation, it had come to such blockings. I don't know how to comment it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was the situation that led to the blocking of the regular armed force of a country? Can you describe the situation a little?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, that's quite difficult. That's quite difficult. It's quite difficult --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I don't think it should be difficult, because you yourself volunteered for this task, to participate in the monitoring mission as a monitor, one of your main tasks was to monitor the ceasefire. You had contacts with all sides, however many sides there were. So please tell me what your opinion is, based on your knowledge of the situation on the ground and what you were told at your briefing and what you were told your task was.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, the situation was quite confusing, and often it was difficult to establish what was going on. So could you specify a little more what you would like me to describe?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why was the JNA blocked in its barracks? What do you know about this? For example, in the city of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, in fact, I don't know much about that, so I'm not able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell us what it was you monitored, what you observed in Zagreb, in Osijek? Can you describe your task in greater detail? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we had a lot of different taskings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For example?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, in Eastern Slavonia, in Osijek, we were monitoring also -- monitoring also ceasefires, and we were -- we did try to contribute to the establishment of ceasefires and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was the problem? Among what sides did the problem arise? Can you tell us with greater precision?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, these problems did occur between Croatian units and JNA units, so it seemed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How well informed are you, and are you well informed, in connection with the job you were doing in that period? Are you in possession of detailed information and reliable information from the areas where you were working?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we -- in connection with our taskings, we got, of course, information about the situation in the areas to which we were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you at some point draw up a report from Osijek about violations of the ceasefire by one of the belligerents?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who you negotiated with there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? In Osijek? Yes, I remember when we were down -- I was down there, we, at one occasion, we went out to the airport, where we had some talks with Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic and Mr. Rade -- the name I don't -- I don't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was their position?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they were members of the government, of Krajina. So they represented themselves, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to any representatives of the army in Osijek? Do you know who was the commander of the barracks in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember that we had talks with some Croatian military persons, but I don't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we had -- I remember that we had two liaison officers from the JNA side, but when we went out to the meeting at the airport, or at other -- oh, yes, yes. We went out to a town outside Osijek, where we had talks with a JNA colonel. So what was his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it Boro Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. Yes, yes, you're right. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who was Rade Sarac?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Rade Sarac. He was one of the liaison officers. I met him as a liaison officer at several occasions. He was at the 5th Military District in Zagreb and went out with us as a liaison officer at some occasions, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did he go to Split with you? And if he did, why?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did. Well, he went with us as a liaison officer. I'm not sure, but it might have been in connection with the first team of the European mission that went to Split. We went there -- yes. Yes. It was on the 24th of September. It's also in my -- in my witness report which I made to the investigators from The Hague two years ago. Yes, it was on the 24th of September we went down to Split. As far as I remember, he went with us at that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was his task? Was he enabling you to pass through the territory as far as Split, or did he have anything to do with the contacts you were supposed to establish in Split?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, he helped us to establish contact with the VPO at Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the military and naval district was in Split at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It was General Mladenic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: While you were working in Zagreb, did you know Adrien Paul Stringer from Great Britain, who was another member of your mission?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I have heard that name, but I can't say that I know him, and I'm not sure that we have had service in the mission at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You say that you went to Split on the 24th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many days before that did you spend in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, you know, at the middle of -- as I told you, at the middle of September I went to Osijek, and as far as I remember, when I came home from Osijek and until I went down to Split, I stayed in Zagreb, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you were in Split, were you establishing an ECMM office or was it a change of shifts with the previous group?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, the team which went down on the 24th of September was -- the first team which went down to Split, and we had the task to establish some kind of presence of the monitoring mission at Split. And we had a press conference, I remember, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that from the 5th to the 10th of October, you were in Dubrovnik for the first time as part of your mission; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would like to know, only briefly, how you reached Dubrovnik. Was this by a civilian vessel or was it a naval vessel?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, it was a civilian vessel. I don't have anything about that in my notes, it seems, but as far as I remember, we went by the ferry boat Slavija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: To Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me: On the 10th, how did you go back from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We also went back by Slavija, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you able to testify at all without consulting your notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems to me that I have already been doing so for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything, without looking at your notes, and yet be certain of what you are saying, without consulting the papers in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Again, it seems to me that I have been doing exactly that for probably at least half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, because the questions were not in connection with the notes you have before you. But let me ask you: Do you have any notes connected to your work in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You only kept notes in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it's quite accidentally I have some notes. Sometimes I didn't have time to make notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. How did you return on the 10th of October from Dubrovnik? Without consulting your notes, if possible, please. On the basis of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we went back to -- well, that's very simple. We went back by ferry boat from Dubrovnik to Rijeka, as far as I remember. And from there, probably some vehicle was waiting for us there or -- and so we went to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the ferry boat, on your way back from Dubrovnik, did you run -- did you meet anyone? Was there a handover with another group? And if so, can you describe this.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, now it seems -- I think that I do remember that the name of that ferry boat was Liburnija, if I'm not mistaken, and I don't remember anything about a handover with another team. So what happened on the trip, as far as I remember, there was an inspection by the JRM. Well, I learned that afterward. I was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Your team, which was in Dubrovnik from the 5th to the 10th, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I think the name was Charlie, Team Charlie, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Whiskey team and who its members were?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember that there was such a team, but I can't remember the name of any member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know, when you left Dubrovnik on the 10th, which team entered Dubrovnik after yours, and did you come across that team?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We might have had a handover with them, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We might have had a handover with the new team coming after us, but I don't remember that. If there was any team after us. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during your first stay in Dubrovnik you persistently tried to meet JNA representatives and that in the end you were not successful in this?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already told here today, our team tried to do that, but we were not successful in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why were you not successful?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I remember that the leader of the team, Mr. Mangan, asked me to make a phone call to the Boka Kotorska, but it was impossible, because all lines were in disorder.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you did not perform your task fully. Did you instruct anyone else to continue this task and to endeavour to contact the JNA?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Now I remember that I was -- I was going to the town hall one day, in order to make arrangements about a ship which should -- on which the next team should go down to the Boka Kotorska.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who did you negotiate with about this boat that was to take them to Boka Kotorska?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I only remember from the city hall that I made a telephone call through the coastal radio, or something like that, but I don't remember with whom I spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was there in the city hall? Who did you talk to and who made it possible for you to get this boat?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, at this special occasion, it seems to me that I was speaking a little with Mr. Sikic about that, but I don't remember details about how we could get this ship.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you able to telephone from there?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was somehow, you know, through the so-called coastal radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And in the city assembly, did they communicate with the JNA through the coastal radio?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Pardon? Could you say it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were Sikic and other representatives of the town assembly communicating with representatives of the JNA through the coastal radio, or did they have this possibility?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, since I could get some connection that way, probably they could do so too. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: While you were there in the town hall, were you in the basement or upstairs?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the town hall is, the location?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, yes. It's in the middle of the Old Town, near the cathedral.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there any type of security for the town hall? Were there guards outside, inside?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the course of your mission in Dubrovnik from the 5th to the 10th of October, and then from the 28th to the 29th of October, and the 4th to the 8th of December, did you ever see anyone in uniform or carrying weapons in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I saw policemen, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where, and how many?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: There were, for example, policemen at our hotel, as guards. I don't remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see policemen in other places as well? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you, during your talks with the representatives of the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff, ask for a meeting with the military forces or military commanders in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I'm not wrong, you said that the task of your mission was to monitor the ceasefire. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, generally spoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. In brief: Doesn't it seem unusual, then, that you, as someone who is an objective observer who has experience in the military and in intelligence, and yet you say in your statement and during your testimony -- or rather, you mention only one side. You never mention a Croatian soldier or a Croatian policeman. And I can see that you were not even interested in reaching the other side. I'm referring to military sides. Isn't that unusual?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, you have to bear in mind that I was just one member of one team.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many members was a team supposed to have in order to carry out the mission you were given?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Usually a team had three members.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian soldiers in the town of Dubrovnik at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I didn't notice any military in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you're monitoring a ceasefire and you know about one side being the JNA, are you also monitoring also the ceasefire between the units of the JNA mutually, or what exactly was the ceasefire that you were monitoring? Between which two sides?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, at this particular time and at that particular place, I'm not sure if there was any ceasefire at all. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there any fire at all? If so, where? Between which two parties? Were the JNA units targeting each other or were there perhaps two, three, or more warring sides? What is it that you learned about the situation specifically?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I have already told you something about some episodes of shelling and so on also during my first day in Dubrovnik. But that's what Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I remember about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Dubrovnik, you seem to have noticed no representatives of the Croatian military. Tell me: During your stay in Dubrovnik, did you ever hear sounds of firing by Croatian artillery?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Crisis Staff mention to you at all that the Dubrovnik side had any military formations?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember anything about that. Your Honours, may I ask permission to supplement a little to what I said before the pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would think there's no objection to that. Yes, Mr. Brolund.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. You said before the pause that the monitorings were only dealing with the JNA side. We were talking about my taskings, the taskings of my team in Osijek. Now I remember one thing which I would like to tell about that. When we were down there in Osijek, in the middle of September, the leader of our town was Colonel Mangan. We offered our good offices to establish a ceasefire, and I remember one occasion when the Croats, so it seems -- seemed to us, did not respect that ceasefire. And I remember at that occasion that we made a protest. We even made a protest to them, Mr. Mangan asked me to call up on the phone to the Croatian side and made -- and make a protest. And so we did. So now I remember in Osijek we had contact with Croatian military also. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you too. May we state that you have no such recollection of events in Dubrovnik? Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember such things in connection with Dubrovnik. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at all during your stay in Dubrovnik, the three times you stayed there, did the JNA ever draw your attention to violations of ceasefire from positions occupied by the Croatian army and from which they were firing on the JNA, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, we have already been mentioning today the letter we got from General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the letter. I'm clear about that. But can you please answer my question, the one I've just asked you.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, exactly in that question, General Strugar said that the Croats had --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please, please. I must interrupt you. You're talking about the letter dated the 6th of December; am I right?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the letter dated the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, in which General Strugar --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please allow me. I know about that letter. I understand the letter. We've looked at it. You've answered those questions. I will ask you additional questions related to that letter; however, my question to you now is: Prior to the 6th of December, during your various stays in Dubrovnik, were there ever any protests being made by the JNA to the effect that Croats, the Croatian army, the Croatian artillery, had fired on JNA units, that they had violated ceasefires? Did the JNA ever warn you about Croatian artillery positions or anything like that? Do you have any knowledge like that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain, in very simple terms, and briefly: You were in Dubrovnik working on what kind of ceasefire exactly? You have the JNA on one side, and who was on the other side, in your view?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, there must have been some Croatian units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is this a logical conclusion you're trying to draw or do you actually know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It's a logical conclusion. I don't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who was the liaison officer on the Croatian side, the one that you were in touch with?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: At Dubrovnik? It seems to me, as far as I remember, that the liaison officer was a person who was in fact working as a translator, Miso. Now I don't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now may I be allowed to remind you, the liaison officer on behalf of the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff, was it Miso Mihocevic, a man named Miso Mihocevic?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It seems to me that he was the liaison person to us from the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have any direct contact with representatives of Dubrovnik's Crisis Staff? If so, with whom precisely, when, and what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: We had meetings with the mayor, Pero Poljanic. As far as I remember, he was the president of the Crisis Staff, and also with Mr. Sikic, who was a member of the Crisis Staff. But I don't remember exactly when these meetings took place. Well, that is, it seems that we had such a meeting when we arrived to Dubrovnik at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: No notes, please. No notes. I'll take you back to your notes when I choose to.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: On the 5th of December, when we -- the day when we arrived. We arrived in the morning. I think that day we had a meeting with the Crisis Staff, but I don't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Your mission and its talks with the Crisis Staff on that day, were your interpretation services used also?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, because Miso was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did Miso get in touch with you on a number of different occasions, in addition to those situations where specifically you talked to members of the Crisis Staff, or rather, the president of Dubrovnik's Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, on the 5th of December, he went with us -- he went with the delegation of ministers and our team to Cavtat. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During your first stay, did you have daily contact with the Crisis Staff in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, the only thing you remember is the day when you first arrived in Dubrovnik with the mission, in relation to your first visit.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That's right. And it's due to the fact that I only have notes about that day. I don't have any notes about the other days. And, after all, it's more than -- it's 12 1/2 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how you gave a statement to the investigators of the Tribunal when you first met them and when you talked about what your testimony today would be.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Pardon? You mean here in The Hague, or when I had the first meeting with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: First meeting you had.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I had the first meeting with the investigators from The Hague in Denmark, in the town where I am living, in April 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this on the 9th and 10th of April, 2002?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you give a statement to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This statement, what was it based on?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was based on what I could remember myself and on my notes, and some notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you gave the statement, did you remember anything at all outside your notes? I mean any essential things for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I remembered, well, some -- most important things, the things, of course, which had left the biggest impression on me. But, after all, a very long period of time has passed, and so a lot of the details had, of course, disappeared from my remembrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you recollect anything that is not actually in your notes? Is there anything like that that's included in the statement?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it seems to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you give an example? During your conversation with -- your interview with the investigators, you used your notes, I assume. Am I correct in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I used the notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Right now, do you remember if there's any part of your statement, the one you gave to the investigators, that's not actually contained in the notes that we reviewed today?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. For example, the fact that Mr. Hvalkof made protests to General Jokic on the 7th of December, in Cavtat, it's nowhere in my notes. I remembered that, for example. That's just one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please, if there are others, can you list them now.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I'm not able to do that in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Because you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I, in this moment, I can't recall the entire text of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Through your entire testimony on examination-in-chief today by my learned friend and colleague - and we find more or less the same thing in the statement that you gave the investigators - despite that, there are things now that you can't remember, things you told them that are not in your notes; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Pardon? Could I have the question once more?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. During the examination-in-chief, you were asked questions by my learned friend and colleague from the Prosecution. You've gone through more or less the entire statement, the statement you had previously given to the investigators. My question now is: As you were using your notes while you were being interviewed, you were using your notes while being asked questions by the Prosecutor here today, is there anything in the statement that you had told the Prosecution that wasn't based on your notes, but rather on your recollection of events from the period?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Your first trip to Dubrovnik on the 5th, who was with you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: It was -- the team was consisting of Colm Mangan, as the leader of the team, and the third -- and then Leif Maersk, and myself, and there was a fourth monitor from Luxembourg whose name I don't remember, and our driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Any of these persons that you have now mentioned by name, are any of them with you in the Hague today?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, they aren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, can you tell me, during your entire stay in Dubrovnik, or rather, the different times that you stayed there, did you move about town a lot?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: To some extent, yes. Not much, but to some extent, at some occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you specify, please. What do you mean by "not much"? What exactly does "not much" mean specifically during your stay?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell how many times we went outside the town. I remember some occasions, of course. I remember we went out to Babin Kuk at one occasion. We went, it seems to me, out to Komolac also.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Babin Kuk, Komolac. Any other places?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember any other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did anyone follow you at the time when you went about?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As you moved about town, were you assisted by anyone external to your own party, any Croats, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: As I told you already, we had Miso as the liaison person, and he also -- he often gave us some assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You told us today that on the 5th of October, you experienced shelling for the very first time. What sort of shelling was it? Who was firing the shells, and where from?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, it was -- the shells fell somewhere between Hotel Argentina and the Old Town. I was together with my colleague Leif Maersk, and it seemed to us that some shells were coming from the sea, and perhaps also some from the land side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was anything hit on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, so about the same place, the next day, I noticed some vehicles, some cars which had burned out, but I'm not sure if they were hit at this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you state this in your notes what specifically was hit during the first shelling that you witnessed on the first day of your stay in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Dubrovnik, before the 10th of October, did anything significant happen? Was anything important going on that you would now perhaps remember? And my question mainly concerns the shelling, firing. Were there any special events that you remember from those days?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember such events.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Your colleague, Hvalkof, did he also take notes at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Your colleague Maersk, whom you socialised with, as I see, did he keep notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was anyone in your mission in charge of keeping notes of day-to-day events of meetings that you had when you met and talked to people?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Of course, every team made a report after every tasking, but that's all I remember about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you specifically: Four monitors are talking, for example, to two lawyers. That is a meeting we're trying to imagine. At that meeting, you can't remember whether anyone is taking notes, you don't know whether anyone is actually taking notes, and you can't remember. Is that what you're trying to tell me now?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Perhaps I will remember, but that's not -- it's a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Following your meetings with the Crisis Staff, with JNA representatives, you people from the mission, did you exchange views on the people you had met and on what had been discussed at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course we did speak about our job with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did the head of your mission also show his views? I have Ambassador Bondioli in mind.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that clearly, but probably to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you make comments concerning your impressions regarding the meeting with representatives of Dubrovnik's crisis staff, Mr. Pero Poljanic, specifically?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many times did you see General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I saw him only once, and that was at the meeting at Meljine on the 28th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And after that --

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I never saw him any more, to my best knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see him on television, in the papers?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to me that I have seen him on the television.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you talk to each other, what did you say about your impressions concerning your meeting with General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the meeting at all, the one on the 28th of October, the one you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Of course I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps choose not to remember anything while answering my questions? Because that is the impression I have.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I'm doing my utmost to tell you everything which I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me one thing, please: Today, in answer to questions by the Prosecutor, you said that during your first stay in Dubrovnik, you had seen a plane firing on the hill of Srdj and that a huge cross, a hilltop cross had been destroyed. Later on, if I'm not mistaken -- let me first ask you if that is correct.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, yes, to my best knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During that round of shelling, the huge hilltop cross on Srdj, was it actually destroyed?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: So I remember it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe your memory of it, what it looked like after the shelling. The hill, was there a cross on top of the hill? Was it broken? Was it totally destroyed? Please describe to the best of your recollection what the hill actually looked like after the shelling.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know which hotel is near Argentina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, yes. It seems to me that Hotel Excelsior is very close, is rather close to Hotel Argentina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Any other hotel nearby?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember any other hotels there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You were there a number of times, not only 1991. Your situation with the local hotel had not changed very much.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't remember any other hotels in that part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you visit Dubrovnik after 1991 to this very day?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there perhaps also Belvedere Hotel nearby? Were you familiar with that hotel?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the name of that hotel, but I don't remember where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did anyone mention to you that there were Croatian military positions near Belvedere Hotel, that's between Argentina Hotel and Belvedere Hotel?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, now I remember from the meeting at Meljine, if I'm not -- as far as I remember, Admiral Jokic said that there were some positions at several places, yes. It's also in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember those positions that General Jokic mentioned?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And on your return from the negotiations with JNA representatives, did you inform the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff about what had been said about the Croatian positions?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you inform anyone about this?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't know. Mr. Bondioli was leader of the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So it seems that Mr. Bondioli would help us a lot more than you can; no offence. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Probably. He was in charge, so of course he will know much more -- he will probably know much more than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When I asked you a little while ago about the large cross on the top of Srdj hill, was it very visible because of its size and its position?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It's very big.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It could even be seen from the sea when approaching Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you enter the fact that that cross was toppled in your notes?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: You know, my notes were often made in a hurry, and so it was accidental what was put in them and what not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In your view, wouldn't that fact be more important, your seeing an enormous cross on Srdj destroyed, than, for example, the fact that a shell fell in a street close to your hotel? Well, I'm just thinking aloud.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, but, as I said just a moment before, it was accidental what was put in my notes and what not. So according to the time, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned these messages, on the 6th of December, the shelling that you talked about took place, and you mentioned two messages, one from Jokic and one from General Strugar; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know when Jokic's message arrived, to whom, and what its contents were?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No. The only thing I have about that in my notes, as I have read for you also today, is that it arrived about 1500 hours. I don't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us whether the message was sent in the form of a telegram or a fax or a phone call or a radio connection? Can you tell us anything about this?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I'm not able to tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this also apply to General Strugar's message which you mentioned as having arrived on the 6th of December? You say that all you have in your notes is 1700 hours, and that's all you can say about it, like this other message.

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: That's all what I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear from anyone, including people from the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff and the members of your mission, that between 1500 hours and 1700 hours, anybody talked either through a radio connection or by telephone, with Admiral Jokic and General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said, while you wrote down Jokic's message 1500 hours, Strugar's message on the same date at 1700 hours. Do you know what the form of these messages was? Were they handwritten? Did they arrive on paper?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Well, according to my notes, the message on 17 -- at 1700 hours from General Strugar was a letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who brought the letter?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know how this letter reached you?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I am not able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know at all where General Strugar was at that time,? On the 6th of December, 1991, where was General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know where his command was?

utterances.speaker: LARS JENSEN BROLUND
